prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1130; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a rear-end collision in which the insured's vehicle was struck from behind while stopped at a traffic signal. Claimant reports a wrist fracture and is represented by counsel, so all contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver is named on it and that coverage was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Photos of the rear bumper and trunk area were obtained from the insured and the claimant's side. They confirm several details of the impact, but no independent witnesses have come forward.

Entry 4: Vehicle damage appears mostly consistent with the impact described by both parties. No prior damage to the vehicle is known from our records or from the repair shop's preliminary notes.

Entry 5: Claimant's account of the collision was given in a recorded statement and again in a follow-up call through counsel. The same sequence of events was described each time.

Entry 6: Medical records received show the wrist fracture and a course of treatment that followed a typical pattern, tapering off as the claimant improved. It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.

Entry 7: Prior records show a small strain in the same area several years ago, which resolved fully. Requested further imaging history to determine whether it bears on the current findings.

Entry 8: Still unclear from the statements and photos exactly where the claimant was seated in the vehicle at impact. Asked counsel to clarify the seating position in writing.

Entry 9: Sent a letter to counsel requesting the outstanding medical bills, the prior treatment records, and the claimant's employment information for the wage loss portion of the claim.

Entry 10: Claim remains open pending receipt of the requested records and the medical review. Next step is to schedule an independent medical review once the prior treatment file arrives.
